The tasks are in [`tasks.json`](tasks.json); results go to `results.md`.

---

## 1. Question

Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP change **whether it can fix a bug in real code** and **how much context it uses doing so**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

- **H1 (context):** with ACC-MCP, the agent's prompts are smaller (lower peak context per model call and fewer total prompt tokens per task), because it reads signature, call-graph, or single-function slices instead of whole files.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP, the agent resolves at least as many tasks as without it, because the slices it gets still contain what it needs.

Both hypotheses are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison.

---

## 2. Why our own benchmark

| Option | Why not used |
| :--- | :--- |
| SWE-bench / SWE-bench Lite | The official grader builds a Docker image per task (several GB each; built locally on Apple Silicon). Too heavy for a 16 GB laptop that also runs the model, and the large repos (Django, sympy) are far beyond a 4B model. |
| Aider / Exercism Python exercises | Each task is one small file. Reading the whole file is cheap, so ACC-MCP has nothing to save and the comparison would only test the agent. |
| HumanEval / MBPP | Single functions with no repository. There is nothing to navigate, so an MCP server for code context is irrelevant. |

What the comparison needs is **real, popular code with files large enough that reading them whole is expensive or impossible**, plus **tests that decide pass/fail automatically without Docker**. The benchmark therefore injects bugs into pinned releases of two well-known pure-Python libraries and grades with their own test suites. This is the bug-injection approach used by SWE-smith: take a working repository, break one function, and ask the agent to repair it from a bug report.

---

## 3. Repositories

| | more-itertools | click |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Source | https://github.com/more-itertools/more-itertools | https://github.com/pallets/click |
| Pinned release | tag `v11.2.1` | tag `8.5.0` |
| License | MIT | BSD-3-Clause |
| What it is | Extra iterator building blocks on top of `itertools` | Command-line interface framework (Pallets) |
| Runtime dependencies | none | none (on macOS/Linux) |
| Package layout | `more_itertools/` at the repo root | `src/click/` (tests need `PYTHONPATH=src`) |
| Test suite | `tests/`, `unittest.TestCase` classes, run with pytest | `tests/`, plain pytest |
| Files with injected bugs | `more_itertools/more.py`: 5,644 lines, ~175 KB | `src/click/core.py`: 3,799 lines; `types.py`: 1,422; `parser.py`: 533; `formatting.py`: 320 |
| Why chosen | `more.py` is about 45K tokens, **larger than the model's ~30K context window**: the agent cannot read it whole and has to find the right function. Hundreds of small, independent functions. | Real class hierarchy (`Command`, `Parameter`, `Option`, `HelpFormatter`) with code split across modules, so callers and callees matter (Tier 2). `core.py` alone is also larger than a comfortable read. |

Both repos are cloned shallowly at the pinned tag (`setup`). Sizes are for these tags.

---

## 4. Tasks

### 4.1 How the tasks were built

1. Pick a function in one of the files above that has its own tests in the repository.
2. Change **one line or one condition** so the function gives wrong results but the code still imports and runs: a swapped argument order, an off-by-one comparison, a flipped condition.
3. Spread the tasks through the files (start, middle, end of `more.py`; four different click modules), so no task is solved by reading the first lines of a file.
4. Write a **bug report** the way a user would file it: what they called, what they got, what they expected. Reports for more-itertools name the public function, as a user would. Reports for click describe only the user-visible behavior and never name the internal function. No report mentions a file, a line, or the code change.
5. Record the tests that cover the function as the task's **target tests**.
6. Check with `validate` that the target tests pass on the original code and fail with the bug (section 4.3).

### 4.2 Task catalogue

| Task | Repo | File (line) | Function | Injected change | Target tests | Bug report (summary) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mi_split_at` | more-itertools | `more.py` (1600) | `split_at` | `if maxsplit == 1:` → `if maxsplit == 2:` | `SplitAtTests` | `maxsplit=2` splits only once; `maxsplit=1` never stops |
| `mi_numeric_range_index` | more-itertools | `more.py` (2476) | `numeric_range.index` | `self._start >= value > self._stop` → `self._start > value > self._stop` | `NumericRangeTests` | `.index()` of the first item of a decreasing range raises `ValueError` |
| `mi_difference` | more-itertools | `more.py` (2940) | `difference` | `map(func, b, a)` → `map(func, a, b)` | `DifferenceTest` | differences come out negated / wrong for custom functions |
| `mi_is_sorted` | more-itertools | `more.py` (4079) | `is_sorted` | strict and non-strict checks swapped | `IsSortedTests` | `is_sorted([1, 2, 2])` is `False`, with `strict=True` it is `True` |
| `mi_constrained_batches` | more-itertools | `more.py` (4981) | `constrained_batches` | `> max_size` → `>= max_size` | `ConstrainedBatchesTests` | items that exactly fill `max_size` are split into two batches |
| `ck_nargs_tuple` | click | `parser.py` (90) | `_unpack_args` | `if spos is not None:` → `if spos is None:` before `x.reverse()` | `test_arguments.py::test_nargs_tup` | `nargs=2` arguments arrive reversed |
| `ck_int_range_min` | click | `types.py` (664) | `_NumberRangeBase.convert` | `operator.le if self.min_open else operator.lt` → the two operators swapped | `test_types.py::test_range` | `IntRange(5)` rejects `5`; `min_open=True` accepts the bound |
| `ck_eager_order` | click | `core.py` (164) | `iter_params_for_processing` | `return not item.is_eager, idx` → `return item.is_eager, idx` | `test_commands.py::test_iter_params_for_processing` | eager options (`--version`, `--help`) run after normal ones |
| `ck_envvar_nargs` | click | `core.py` (2725) | `Parameter.value_from_envvar` | `self.nargs != 1` → `self.nargs > 1` | `test_arguments.py::test_nargs_envvar` | a `nargs=-1` argument no longer splits its environment variable |
| `ck_help_columns` | click | `formatting.py` (255) | `HelpFormatter.write_dl` | `term_len(first) <= ...` → `term_len(first) < ...` | `test_formatting.py` | in `--help`, the longest option's description wraps to the next line |

Exact before/after strings and full bug reports are in `tasks.json`. more-itertools test classes are in `tests/test_more.py`.

### 4.3 Validation (before any run)

`python3 eval/pi_bench.py validate`:
1. Runs each repository's full test suite on the clean code and stores the failing tests, if any, as the **baseline** (`eval/work/baseline/<repo>.json`). These are not counted against the agent later.
2. For each task, checks that the "before" string occurs exactly once in the file, that the target tests pass on the clean code, and that at least one target test fails with the bug.

A task that fails validation is fixed or dropped before running the benchmark.

---

## 5. Conditions

Each task runs once in each of two modes. The **only** differences between the modes are the ACC-MCP server and one hint sentence.

### 5.1 Held constant in both modes

| Item | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Model | Qwen3.5-4B GGUF served by `llama-server` at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. The exact file is printed by `doctor` and must be recorded with the results. |
| Context window | per-slot `n_ctx` read from `llama-server /props` (30,208 on the reference machine), given to Pi as the model's `contextWindow` |
| Max output per call | 4,096 tokens |
| Agent | Pi coding agent in its normal **interactive** terminal UI, opened by the operator with the task's `start.sh` |
| Tools | Pi's defaults: `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write` |
| Pi configuration | a fresh `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` per run containing only `models.json`, `settings.json` (and `mcp.json` in acc mode). The user's own MCP servers, skills, prompt templates, themes and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` files are not loaded (`--no-context-files --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-themes`). |
| Compaction | on, `reserveTokens` 4,096, `keepRecentTokens` 8,000 (Pi's default reserve of 16,384 would leave little of a 30K window) |
| Prompt | the same template for every task: the bug report, "find the cause in the library source code and fix it, do not modify or add tests, you can run the tests with `python -m pytest <path>`, reply with one sentence" |
| Workspace | a fresh copy of the pinned repo with the bug committed as its only commit |
| Python for the agent's commands | `eval/work/venv` (Python 3.12 + pytest), first on `PATH`; `PYTHONPATH=src` for click |
| Time limit | 30 minutes per run (operator stops the run, section 6.1) |
| Order | for each task, plain then acc, so slow drift (heat, other load, the operator getting used to a task) affects both modes alike |

### 5.2 The treatment (acc mode only)

- ACC-MCP is started by Pi as a stdio MCP server (`.venv/bin/python -m acc_mcp.server`) with `direct` exposure, so its tools are declared to the model like built-in tools: `mcp__acc_mcp__get_adaptive_context`, `mcp__acc_mcp__find_symbol`, `mcp__acc_mcp__get_token_ledger`, `mcp__acc_mcp__reset_session`.
- `ACC_MCP_ROOT` = the task workspace; `ACC_MCP_LEDGER` = a per-run file outside the workspace; session budget 6,000 tokens.
- One sentence is appended to the system prompt (`ACC_HINT` in `pi_bench.py`): prefer `find_symbol` and `get_adaptive_context` over reading whole files, and call again with `min_tier=3` if a slice is not enough.
- The built-in tools stay available, so the agent can always fall back to `read` and `bash`.

`--no-hint` runs acc mode without the sentence, to separate the effect of the tools from the effect of the instruction.

---

## 6. Procedure for one run

The runs are done by hand: the operator opens Pi, gives the model the task, watches it work, and stops. The script only prepares the run beforehand and measures it afterwards.

1. **Prepare** (`pi_bench.py prepare <task> --mode <plain|acc>`): copy the pinned repo into `eval/work/runs/<run-id>/<mode>/<task>/workspace/` without `.git`, inject the bug, `git init`, commit everything as "Initial commit" (test caches are hidden via `.git/info/exclude`). Write the isolated Pi configuration (section 5), `start.sh`, and `prompt.txt`.
2. **Open Pi**: `bash .../start.sh`. It changes into the workspace, sets the Pi config folder, the test venv and (click) `PYTHONPATH`, and starts interactive Pi with the local model; acc mode also appends the hint.
3. **Give the task**: paste `prompt.txt` as the first message, unchanged.
4. **Watch** the model work, following the operator rules below.
5. **Quit Pi** when a stop condition is met.
6. **Collect** (`pi_bench.py collect <task> --mode <...> --notes "..."`): read Pi's session file and, in acc mode, the ACC-MCP ledger; save the model's code changes (`patch.diff`, tests excluded) and whether it touched `tests/`; restore `tests/`; run the target tests and the full suite; write `result.json` with the operator's notes.

### 6.1 Operator rules

The operator is part of the experiment, so the same rules apply in both modes:

- Send the prompt from `prompt.txt` unchanged as the first message. Do not add hints about the file, the function, or the fix.
- If the model asks a question, answer only: `Proceed as you think best.`
- If the model stops before saying it is done (for example it only describes a plan), send `Continue.` At most 3 times per run.
- Do not edit files, run commands in the workspace, or approve anything outside what Pi asks for itself.
- **Stop** (quit Pi) when the model says it is done, when it has been stuck in the same loop for about 5 minutes, after the third `Continue.`, or at 30 minutes.
- Write down in `--notes` what you saw: how it searched for the code, wrong turns, whether it used ACC-MCP, errors, why you stopped.

The number of operator messages is counted from the session (`user_messages`), so extra nudges are visible in the results.

---

## 7. Grading

A task is **resolved** when, after step 5:
- every target test passes (at least one ran), and
- the full suite has no failing test that was not already failing on the clean repo (the baseline from `validate`).

Also recorded: whether the agent changed the file that contains the bug, which files it changed, and whether it edited tests. The operator's notes record why the run was stopped.

---

## 8. Metrics

| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Resolved | section 7 | test runs |
| Model calls | number of assistant responses (one per agent step) | Pi session file (`sessions/*.jsonl`), assistant messages |
| Peak context | largest prompt of a single model call: input + cache-read + cache-write tokens, as llama-server reports them to Pi. Directly comparable to the context window. | `usage` of each assistant message |
| Total prompt tokens | sum of the prompt sizes over all calls: how much context the model processed for the whole task | same |
| Output tokens | tokens generated | same |
| Tool calls / tool output | number of calls and characters returned, per tool | tool-result messages in the session |
| Compactions | times Pi had to summarize the conversation to stay in the window | compaction entries in the session |
| Operator messages | messages the operator sent (1 = only the prompt) | user messages in the session |
| Minutes | time from the first to the last message | session timestamps |
| Operator notes | what the operator observed and why the run stopped | `collect --notes` |
| ACC-MCP requests, tiers | requests served and their tier (1/2/3), and the tier the decision model picked | ACC-MCP ledger |
| Escalations | requests where the agent raised `min_tier` above the model's tier | ACC-MCP ledger |
| Budget step-downs / refusals | slices served one tier lower, or refused, because the session budget was nearly used up | ledger and tool output |
| ACC-MCP tokens vs whole file | tokens served vs tokens of the whole files those slices came from | ACC-MCP ledger |

---

## 9. Analysis

- **Per mode:** resolved count out of 10, and the median of peak context, total prompt tokens, model calls and wall time.
- **Per task (paired):** the same task in both modes, side by side in `results.md`, so a difference can be traced to what the agent did (tools used, tiers served, escalations).
- **Was ACC-MCP used at all?** The number of acc runs in which the model actually called an ACC-MCP tool. If a 4B model ignores the tools, the acc runs measure Pi alone, and that is itself a result.
- With 10 tasks and one run each, a difference of one or two resolved tasks is within noise. To see the spread, repeat the whole run with a new `--run-id` and report each run, not only the best.
- Results are reported as they come out, including if ACC-MCP makes things worse.

---

## 10. Threats to validity

- **Small sample:** 10 tasks, one run per task and mode by default.
- **Injected bugs:** single-line changes are easier to localize than real bugs and may not represent real maintenance work. The reports were written by the project author.
- **Training data:** both libraries are popular and likely in the model's training data, so the model may recognize the code. This affects both modes equally but can inflate the success rate.
- **Sampling:** the model's sampling is not seeded; reruns differ.
- **Operator effect:** a person runs Pi and decides when to stop. The operator rules (6.1) limit this, and every extra message is counted, but the operator knows the bug and could steer unconsciously. Ideally the operator does not read the injected change in `tasks.json` before running.
- **Hint confound:** acc mode adds one instruction sentence; `--no-hint` runs separate its effect from the tools'.
- **Token accounting:** context numbers are what llama-server reports to Pi. ACC-MCP's own counts use a different tokenizer (tiktoken or a character estimate), so its tokens and Pi's are compared only within their own source.
- **One machine, one model:** results hold for this model file, quantization and context size.

---

## 11. Running it

From the repository root, with the model already running on port 8080:

One-time preparation:

```bash
uv sync                                   # ACC-MCP must be importable from .venv
python3 eval/pi_bench.py setup            # clone both repos at their tags, create eval/work/venv
python3 eval/pi_bench.py validate         # baseline + all 10 tasks must be OK
python3 eval/pi_bench.py doctor           # model, Pi version; acc-mcp must be connected with 4 tools
```

For each task, plain first, then acc:

```bash
python3 eval/pi_bench.py prepare mi_difference --mode plain     # prints the next steps and the prompt
bash eval/work/runs/run1/plain/mi_difference/start.sh           # interactive Pi; paste the prompt; quit when done
python3 eval/pi_bench.py collect mi_difference --mode plain --notes "found it with grep, fixed in 6 steps"

python3 eval/pi_bench.py prepare mi_difference --mode acc
bash eval/work/runs/run1/acc/mi_difference/start.sh
python3 eval/pi_bench.py collect mi_difference --mode acc --notes "..."
```

Progress and results:

```bash
python3 eval/pi_bench.py list             # which task/mode pairs are prepared or collected
python3 eval/pi_bench.py report           # writes eval/results.md
```

Use `--run-id` for a repeat of the whole set, and `prepare --mode acc --no-hint` to try ACC-MCP without the hint sentence. Everything for one run is in `eval/work/runs/<run-id>/<mode>/<task>/`: `start.sh`, `prompt.txt`, `sessions/` (Pi session), `acc_ledger.json`, `patch.diff`, `junit_target.xml`, `junit_full.xml`, `result.json`.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cmd_setup(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    data = load_tasks()
    REPOS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for name, repo in data["repos"].items():
        dst = REPOS_DIR / name
        if dst.exists():
            print(f"[setup] {name}: already at {dst}")
            continue
        print(f"[setup] cloning {repo['url']} @ {repo['tag']}")
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--branch", repo["tag"], repo["url"], str(dst)], check=True)
    if not (VENV_DIR / "bin" / "python").exists():
        print(f"[setup] creating test venv at {VENV_DIR}")
        subprocess.run(["uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", "3.12", str(VENV_DIR)], check=True)
    subprocess.run(["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "--python", str(VENV_DIR / "bin" / "python"), "pytest"], check=True)
    print("[setup] done. Next: python3 eval/pi_bench.py validate")
    return 0


def cmd_validate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Record each repo's already-failing tests, then check each injected bug breaks its tests."""
    data = load_tasks()
    scratch = WORK_DIR / "validate"
    BASELINE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ok = True
    for name, repo in data["repos"].items():
        ws = make_workspace(REPOS_DIR / name, scratch / name, None)
        full = run_pytest(ws, [repo["test_dir"]], tool_env(repo, ws), scratch / f"{name}.xml")
        (BASELINE_DIR / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"passed": full.passed, "failed_ids": full.failed_ids}, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"[validate] {name}: clean suite {full.passed} passed, {full.failed} failed (baseline)")
    for task in data["tasks"]:
        repo = data["repos"][task["repo"]]
        clean = make_workspace(REPOS_DIR / task["repo"], scratch / task["id"] / "clean", None)
        before = run_pytest(clean, task["tests"], tool_env(repo, clean), scratch / task["id"] / "clean.xml")
        try:
            broken = make_workspace(REPOS_DIR / task["repo"], scratch / task["id"] / "broken", task)
        except ValueError as exc:
            print(f"[validate] {task['id']}: INVALID - {exc}")
            ok = False
            continue
        after = run_pytest(broken, task["tests"], tool_env(repo, broken), scratch / task["id"] / "broken.xml")
        valid = before.passed > 0 and before.failed == 0 and after.failed > 0
        ok &= valid
        print(f"[validate] {task['id']}: {'OK     ' if valid else 'INVALID'} original {before.passed} passed/"
              f"{before.failed} failed, with bug {after.passed} passed/{after.failed} failed")
    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    print("[validate] all tasks valid" if ok else "[validate] some tasks are invalid")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def cmd_doctor(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Check the model endpoint, Pi, and that Pi can start ACC-MCP over stdio."""
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{args.endpoint}/v1/models", timeout=5) as resp:
            print(f"[doctor] llama-server model: {json.load(resp)['data'][0]['id']}")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[doctor] llama-server not reachable at {args.endpoint}: {exc}")
        return 1
    print(f"[doctor] context window per slot: {query_context_window(args.endpoint)}")
    version = subprocess.run(["pi", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"[doctor] pi {version.stdout.strip() or version.stderr.strip()}")
    probe = WORK_DIR / "doctor"
    first = next(iter(load_tasks()["repos"]))
    ws = make_workspace(REPOS_DIR / first, probe / "workspace", None)
    write_agent_dir(probe / "pi-agent", "acc", ws, probe / "ledger.json", query_context_window(args.endpoint), args.endpoint)
    listing = subprocess.run(["pi", "mcp", "list"], cwd=ws, env=dict(os.environ, PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=str(probe / "pi-agent")),
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(listing.stdout + listing.stderr)
    shutil.rmtree(probe, ignore_errors=True)
    return listing.returncode


def cmd_prepare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    data = load_tasks()
    task = find_task(data, args.task)
    repo = data["repos"][task["repo"]]
    out_dir = run_dir_for(args.run_id, args.mode, task["id"])
    if out_dir.exists() and not args.force:
        print(f"[prepare] {out_dir} already exists; use --force to start this task over")
        return 1
    if out_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True)

    workspace = make_workspace(REPOS_DIR / task["repo"], out_dir / "workspace", task)
    context_window = query_context_window(args.endpoint)
    write_agent_dir(out_dir / "pi-agent", args.mode, workspace, out_dir / "acc_ledger.json",
                    context_window, args.endpoint, args.session_budget)
    (out_dir / "sessions").mkdir()
    hint = args.mode == "acc" and not args.no_hint
    script = out_dir / "start.sh"
    script.write_text(start_script(repo, workspace, out_dir / "pi-agent", out_dir / "sessions", args.mode, hint), encoding="utf-8")
    script.chmod(0o755)
    prompt = build_prompt(task)
    (out_dir / "prompt.txt").write_text(prompt + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (out_dir / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "task": task["id"], "repo": task["repo"], "mode": args.mode, "hint": hint,
        "context_window": context_window, "session_budget": args.session_budget if args.mode == "acc" else None,
        "prepared_at": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"[prepare] {task['id']} ({args.mode}) ready, context window {context_window}\n")
    print(f"1. Open Pi:\n\n   bash {script}\n")

def write_metadata_stub(repo_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Metadata-only `<name>-<version>.dist-info` for a src-layout repo, in the test venv.

    Such a repo is imported through PYTHONPATH, not installed, so
    `importlib.metadata.version("click")` raises PackageNotFoundError; click's
    tests/test_deprecations.py calls it while pytest collects, which aborted the whole
    clean suite (0 tests passed). The stub has no code, so the package is still imported
    only from the workspace: a fix the agent makes is what the tests run.
    """
    pyproject = repo_dir / "pyproject.toml"
    if not pyproject.exists():
        return None
    project = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("project", {})
    name, version = project.get("name"), project.get("version")
    site = next(VENV_DIR.glob("lib/python*/site-packages"), None)
    if not name or not version or site is None:
        return None
    dist = site / f"{name.replace('-', '_')}-{version}.dist-info"
    dist.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (dist / "METADATA").write_text(f"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: {name}\nVersion: {version}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    (dist / "INSTALLER").write_text("pi_bench (metadata only, no code)\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return dist

input.old_string:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP change **whether it can fix a bug in real code** and **how much context it uses doing so**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

- **H1 (context):** with ACC-MCP, the agent's prompts are smaller (lower peak context per model call and fewer total prompt tokens per task), because it reads signature, call-graph, or single-function slices instead of whole files.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP, the agent resolves at least as many tasks as without it, because the slices it gets still contain what it needs.

Both hypotheses are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison.
input.new_string:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP make it **cheaper to find and read the code it needs**, without making it **worse at fixing the bug**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

The comparison is against what the agent really does without ACC-MCP, not against reading whole files. In the pilot session (section 9) the agent found the function with `grep -n` and read it in 10-100 line windows with `read`; it never loaded the ~45K-token file. So the baseline is the agent's own `grep` + windowed `read` strategy.

- **H1 (navigation cost):** with ACC-MCP the agent needs **fewer navigation calls** before it edits the target function, and **fewer code-reading tokens** (output of `read`, `grep`, `sed`, ... plus ACC-MCP slices) than with its own `grep` + `read` strategy.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP the agent resolves **at least as many** tasks as without it.
- **H3 (peak context):** with ACC-MCP the largest prompt of a single model call is smaller. This may not change: in the pilot most of the context came from the agent's own Python experiments (`python3 -c ...`), not from reading code, and ACC-MCP does not touch those.

All three are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison. The metrics behind them are defined in section 8.

input.new_string:
1. Pick a function in one of the files above that has its own tests in the repository.
2. Change **one line or one condition** so the function gives wrong results but the code still imports and runs: a swapped argument order, an off-by-one comparison, a flipped condition.
3. Spread the tasks through the files (start, middle, end of `more.py`; four different click modules), so no task is solved by reading the first lines of a file.
4. Write a **bug report**: what was called, what came out, what was expected, with a small example. Reports for more-itertools name the public function. Reports for click name the public API involved and the module (`src/click/<module>.py`), but not the buggy function. No report mentions a line or the code change. The reports were made easier after the pilot (Phase 25), because the 4B model struggled with vaguer ones even at Q6.
5. Record the tests that cover the function as the task's **target tests**.
6. Check with `validate` that the target tests pass on the original code and fail with the bug (section 4.3).

There are two kinds of task (`kind` in `tasks.json`):

- **`direct`** (6 tasks): the report names or clearly points at the function that has the bug. The agent has to find it in a large file and fix it.
- **`call_graph`** (4 tasks): the report names an **entry** function (`entry` in `tasks.json`) that behaves wrongly, but the bug is in a helper that the entry function calls. The report says so ("the function only chooses a helper", "the order comes from a helper"), but never names the helper. The agent has to follow the call graph from the entry function to the helper. These tasks exist because in bug fixes where the report points at the function itself, the decision model almost always picks Tier 3, so Tier 1 and Tier 2 (signatures and callees) would barely be exercised.

toolUseResult.oldString:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP change **whether it can fix a bug in real code** and **how much context it uses doing so**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

- **H1 (context):** with ACC-MCP, the agent's prompts are smaller (lower peak context per model call and fewer total prompt tokens per task), because it reads signature, call-graph, or single-function slices instead of whole files.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP, the agent resolves at least as many tasks as without it, because the slices it gets still contain what it needs.

Both hypotheses are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison.
toolUseResult.newString:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP make it **cheaper to find and read the code it needs**, without making it **worse at fixing the bug**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

The comparison is against what the agent really does without ACC-MCP, not against reading whole files. In the pilot session (section 9) the agent found the function with `grep -n` and read it in 10-100 line windows with `read`; it never loaded the ~45K-token file. So the baseline is the agent's own `grep` + windowed `read` strategy.

- **H1 (navigation cost):** with ACC-MCP the agent needs **fewer navigation calls** before it edits the target function, and **fewer code-reading tokens** (output of `read`, `grep`, `sed`, ... plus ACC-MCP slices) than with its own `grep` + `read` strategy.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP the agent resolves **at least as many** tasks as without it.
- **H3 (peak context):** with ACC-MCP the largest prompt of a single model call is smaller. This may not change: in the pilot most of the context came from the agent's own Python experiments (`python3 -c ...`), not from reading code, and ACC-MCP does not touch those.

All three are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison. The metrics behind them are defined in section 8.

2. Change **one line or one condition** so the function gives wrong results but the code still imports and runs: a swapped argument order, an off-by-one comparison, a flipped condition.

Reports for click name the public API involved and the module (`src/click/<module>.py`), but not the buggy function. No report mentions a line or the code change. The reports were made easier after the pilot (Phase 25), because the 4B model struggled with vaguer ones even at Q6.

There are two kinds of task (`kind` in `tasks.json`):

- **`direct`** (6 tasks): the report names or clearly points at the function that has the bug. The agent has to find it in a large file and fix it.
- **`call_graph`** (4 tasks): the report names an **entry** function (`entry` in `tasks.json`) that behaves wrongly, but the bug is in a helper that the entry function calls. The report says so ("the function only chooses a helper", "the order comes from a helper"), but never names the helper. The agent has to follow the call graph from the entry function to the helper. These tasks exist because in bug fixes where the report points at the function itself, the decision model almost always picks Tier 3, so Tier 1 and Tier 2 (signatures and callees) would barely be exercised.

input.old_string:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP change **whether it can fix a bug in real code** and **how much context it uses doing so**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

- **H1 (context):** with ACC-MCP, the agent's prompts are smaller (lower peak context per model call and fewer total prompt tokens per task), because it reads signature, call-graph, or single-function slices instead of whole files.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP, the agent resolves at least as many tasks as without it, because the slices it gets still contain what it needs.

Both hypotheses are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison.
input.new_string:
Does giving a small local model ACC-MCP make it **cheaper to find and read the code it needs**, without making it **worse at fixing the bug**, when the model works inside a real coding agent?

The comparison is against what the agent really does without ACC-MCP, not against reading whole files. In the pilot session (section 9) the agent found the function with `grep -n` and read it in 10-100 line windows with `read`; it never loaded the ~45K-token file. So the baseline is the agent's own `grep` + windowed `read` strategy.

- **H1 (navigation cost):** with ACC-MCP the agent needs **fewer navigation calls** before it edits the target function, and **fewer code-reading tokens** (output of `read`, `grep`, `sed`, ... plus ACC-MCP slices) than with its own `grep` + `read` strategy.
- **H2 (success):** with ACC-MCP the agent resolves **at least as many** tasks as without it.
- **H3 (peak context):** with ACC-MCP the largest prompt of a single model call is smaller. This may not change: in the pilot most of the context came from the agent's own Python experiments (`python3 -c ...`), not from reading code, and ACC-MCP does not touch those.

All three are checked on the same tasks, so each task gives a paired comparison. The metrics behind them are defined in section 8.

input.new_string:
1. Pick a function in one of the files above that has its own tests in the repository.
2. Change **one line or one condition** so the function gives wrong results but the code still imports and runs: a swapped argument order, an off-by-one comparison, a flipped condition.
3. Spread the tasks through the files (start, middle, end of `more.py`; four different click modules), so no task is solved by reading the first lines of a file.
4. Write a **bug report**: what was called, what came out, what was expected, with a small example. Reports for more-itertools name the public function. Reports for click name the public API involved and the module (`src/click/<module>.py`), but not the buggy function. No report mentions a line or the code change. The reports were made easier after the pilot (Phase 25), because the 4B model struggled with vaguer ones even at Q6.
5. Record the tests that cover the function as the task's **target tests**.
6. Check with `validate` that the target tests pass on the original code and fail with the bug (section 4.3).

There are two kinds of task (`kind` in `tasks.json`):

- **`direct`** (6 tasks): the report names or clearly points at the function that has the bug. The agent has to find it in a large file and fix it.
- **`call_graph`** (4 tasks): the report names an **entry** function (`entry` in `tasks.json`) that behaves wrongly, but the bug is in a helper that the entry function calls. The report says so ("the function only chooses a helper", "the order comes from a helper"), but never names the helper. The agent has to follow the call graph from the entry function to the helper. These tasks exist because in bug fixes where the report points at the function itself, the decision model almost always picks Tier 3, so Tier 1 and Tier 2 (signatures and callees) would barely be exercised.

input.new_string:
1. Runs each repository's full test suite on the clean code and stores the failing tests, if any, as the **baseline** (`eval/work/baseline/<repo>.json`). These are not counted against the agent later. **A clean suite that passes 0 tests fails validation**, because then the "no new failures" check in section 7 would compare against nothing.
2. For each task, checks that the "before" string occurs exactly once in the file, that the target tests pass on the clean code, and that at least one target test fails with the bug.

A task that fails validation is fixed or dropped before running the benchmark.

**Click baseline fix (Phase 25).** Before this fix the clean click suite passed 0 tests: `tests/test_deprecations.py` calls `importlib.metadata.version("click")` while pytest collects it, and click is imported through `PYTHONPATH=src` instead of being installed, so the call raised `PackageNotFoundError` and pytest stopped the whole run. `setup` now writes a **metadata-only** `click-8.5.0.dist-info` (name and version, no code) into the test venv. Version lookups work, and click is still imported only from the workspace, so the tests always run the agent's version of the code.

input.old_string:
| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Resolved | section 7 | test runs |
| Model calls | number of assistant responses (one per agent step) | Pi session file (`sessions/*.jsonl`), assistant messages |
| Peak context | largest prompt of a single model call: input + cache-read + cache-write tokens, as llama-server reports them to Pi. Directly comparable to the context window. | `usage` of each assistant message |

| Escalations | requests where the agent raised `min_tier` above the model's tier | ACC-MCP ledger |

input.new_string:
All metrics come from files written during the run (Pi's session file, the ACC-MCP ledger, the test results), so measuring costs the operator nothing. `collect` computes them and stores them in `result.json`.

**Navigation (H1).** Every tool call is put in one class: **code_read** (Pi's `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, and bash commands whose pipeline starts with `grep`, `rg`, `sed`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `awk`, `nl`, `find` or `ls`), **acc** (any ACC-MCP tool), **test_run** (`pytest`, `python -m pytest`/`unittest`, `tox`, `nox`), **edit** (`edit`, `write`, `sed -i`), and **other** (everything else, mostly the agent's own Python experiments). Output tokens are counted with **one counter for both modes**, characters / 3.8, so plain and acc numbers are directly comparable. The target function's line range is read with `ast` from the clean repository.

| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Navigation calls before the target edit | code_read calls plus ACC-MCP `find_symbol` / `get_adaptive_context` calls made before the first edit that changes a line of the target function (edited lines come from Pi's edit patch). Empty if the target was never edited. **Primary H1 metric.** | session file + clean repo |
| Code-reading tokens | output tokens of code_read calls plus ACC-MCP slices (`acc`). **Primary H1 metric.** | session file |
| Tokens per class | output tokens of code_read, acc, test_run, edit, other calls | session file |
| Read windows / wasted reads | windows the agent read itself (`read` offset..offset+limit, `sed -n a,bp`, `head`, `cat`); wasted = windows that do not overlap the target function, including any other file | session file + clean repo |
| Large reads | single code_read or acc calls that returned more than 4,000 tokens: measures whether the agent really reads whole files instead of assuming it | session file |

**Context and effort (H3).**

| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Peak context | largest prompt of a single model call: input + cache-read + cache-write tokens, as llama-server reports them to Pi. Directly comparable to the 30,208-token window. **Primary H3 metric.** | `usage` of each assistant message |
| Total prompt tokens | sum of the prompt sizes over all calls: how much context the model processed for the whole task | same |
| Model calls, output tokens | assistant responses and tokens generated | same |
| Tool calls / tool output | number of calls and characters returned, per tool | tool-result messages in the session |
| Compactions | times Pi had to summarize the conversation to stay in the window | compaction entries in the session |
| Operator messages | messages the operator sent (1 = only the prompt) | user messages in the session |
| Minutes | time from the first to the last message | session timestamps |

**Success (H2).** Resolved (section 7), whether the buggy file was edited, whether tests were edited, and the operator's notes (`collect --notes`).

**ACC-MCP (acc mode only).**

| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Requests, tiers | slices served, their tier (1/2/3), and the tier the decision model picked | ACC-MCP ledger |
| Explicit escalations | requests where the agent raised `min_tier` above the model's tier | ACC-MCP ledger |
| Silent escalations | Tier 1 or Tier 2 slices after which the agent read some of the same lines itself (`read`, `sed -n`, `head`, `cat`) within the next 5 tool calls: the slice was not enough, but the agent did not say so through `min_tier` | ledger line ranges + session file |
| Online miss rate | (explicit + silent escalations) / slices served: the decision model's miss rate on real use, next to its offline holdout result (Block 4) | both |
| Budget step-downs / refusals | slices served one tier lower, or refused, because the session budget was nearly used up | ledger and tool output |
| Whole-file tokens | tokens of the whole files the slices came from. **An upper bound only**: agents read windows, not whole files, so this is not a measured saving and is not used for any hypothesis. | ACC-MCP ledger |

- **Per mode:** resolved count out of 10, and the median of peak context, total prompt tokens, model calls and wall time.
- **Per task (paired):** the same task in both modes, side by side in `results.md`, so a difference can be traced to what the agent did (tools used, tiers served, escalations).
- **Was ACC-MCP used at all?** The number of acc runs in which the model actually called an ACC-MCP tool. If a 4B model ignores the tools, the acc runs measure Pi alone, and that is itself a result.
- With 10 tasks and one run each, a difference of one or two resolved tasks is within noise. To see the spread, repeat the whole run with a new `--run-id` and report each run, not only the best.
- Results are reported as they come out, including if ACC-MCP makes things worse.
input.new_string:
- **Pilot excluded.** The pilot session (`eval/work/runs/run1/plain/mi_difference`) was run before the metrics, the click baseline and the tasks were fixed, and `mi_difference` is no longer a task. - **Injected bugs:** single-line changes are easier to localize than real bugs and may not represent real maintenance work. All metrics come from files written during the run (Pi's session file, the ACC-MCP ledger, the test results), so measuring costs the operator nothing. `collect` computes them and stores them in `result.json`.

**Navigation (H1).** Every tool call is put in one class: **code_read** (Pi's `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, and bash commands whose pipeline starts with `grep`, `rg`, `sed`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `awk`, `nl`, `find` or `ls`), **acc** (any ACC-MCP tool), **test_run** (`pytest`, `python -m pytest`/`unittest`, `tox`, `nox`), **edit** (`edit`, `write`, `sed -i`), and **other** (everything else, mostly the agent's own Python experiments). Output tokens are counted with **one counter for both modes**, characters / 3.8, so plain and acc numbers are directly comparable. The target function's line range is read with `ast` from the clean repository.

| Metric | Definition | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Navigation calls before the target edit | code_read calls plus ACC-MCP `find_symbol` / `get_adaptive_context` calls made before the first edit that changes a line of the target function (edited lines come from Pi's edit patch). Empty if the target was never edited. **Primary H1 metric.** | session file + clean repo |
| Code-reading tokens | output tokens of code_read calls plus ACC-MCP slices (`acc`). **Primary H1 metric.** | session file |
| Tokens per class | output tokens of code_read, acc, test_run, edit, other calls | session file |
| Read windows / wasted reads | windows the agent read itself (`read` offset..offset+limit, `sed -n a,bp`, `head`, `cat`); wasted = windows that do not overlap the target function, including any other file | session file + clean repo |
| Large reads | single code_read or acc calls that returned more than 4,000 tokens: measures whether the agent really reads whole files instead of assuming it | session file |

| Metric | Definition | Source |

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Formulation

Small local models such as **Qwen3.5-4B** run with a small context window on a laptop (this project assumes 8,192 tokens). A coding agent that reads whole source files into that window fills it quickly:
1. **Context bloat:** a full window leaves less room for the task, and an overfull request fails outright.
2. **Token waste:** many questions (checking a signature, a type hint, or who calls a function) need only the interface, not the function bodies.

**Adaptive Context Compressor (ACC-MCP)** is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that sits between the agent and the code. Instead of returning raw files, a **Decision Model** picks how much of a symbol to show (signatures, call graph, or full body) and serves that slice of the file. Rules written in code enforce a token ceiling, a per-session token budget, and which files may be read at all.

---

16	## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Formulation
17	
18	Small local models such as **Qwen3.5-4B** run with a small context window on a laptop (this project assumes 8,192 tokens). A coding agent that reads whole source files into that window fills it quickly:
19	1. **Context bloat:** a full window leaves less room for the task, and an overfull request fails outright.
20	2. **Token waste:** many questions (checking a signature, a type hint, or who calls a function) need only the interface, not the function bodies.
21	
22	**Adaptive Context Compressor (ACC-MCP)** is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that sits between the agent and the code. Instead of returning raw files, a **Decision Model** picks how much of a symbol to show (signatures, call graph, or full body) and serves that slice of the file. Rules written in code enforce a token ceiling, a per-session token budget, and which files may be read at all.

### Block 5: Memory or Context Budget Management (`src/acc_mcp/budget.py`, `src/acc_mcp/index.py`)

-- **Session Budget:** All slices in a session share a token budget (`ACC_MCP_SESSION_BUDGET`, default 6,000 tokens). Each slice is cut to $\min(C_{\max}, \text{tokens left})$. def _median(values: list[float]) -> float:
    return round(statistics.median(values), 1) if values else 0


def render_report(results: list[dict[str, Any]], run_id: str) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# Pi Benchmark Results (run `{run_id}`)", "",
        "Plain Pi vs Pi + ACC-MCP, operated by hand in interactive Pi (method: `eval/PROTOCOL.md`).",
        "Context = whole prompt of one model call (input + cached tokens, from Pi's session file).", "",
        "## Summary", "",
        "| Mode | Runs | Resolved | Median peak context | Median prompt tokens / task | Median model calls | Median minutes |",
        "| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |",
    ]
    for mode in MODES:
        rs = [r for r in results if r["mode"] == mode]
        if rs:
            lines.append(
                f"| {mode} | {len(rs)} | {sum(r['grade']['resolved'] for r in rs)}/{len(rs)} "
                f"| {_median([r['pi']['peak_context_tokens'] for r in rs]):g} "
                f"| {_median([r['pi']['total_prompt_tokens'] for r in rs]):g} "
                f"| {_median([r['pi']['model_calls'] for r in rs]):g} "
                f"| {_median([r['pi']['minutes'] for r in rs]):g} |"
            )
    acc = [r for r in results if r["mode"] == "acc"]
    if acc:
        used = sum(1 for r in acc if r["acc"] and r["acc"]["requests"])
        lines += ["", f"ACC-MCP was actually called in {used} of {len(acc)} acc runs."]
    lines += [
        "", "## Per Task", "",
        "| Task | Mode | Resolved | Calls | Peak ctx | Prompt tokens | Tools used | ACC tiers 1/2/3 | Escalations | Min | Notes |",
        "| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |",
    ]
    for r in sorted(results, key=lambda r: (r["task"], r["mode"])):
        p, g, a = r["pi"], r["grade"], r["acc"]
        tools = ", ".join(f"{k.replace('mcp__acc_mcp__', 'acc:')}×{v}" for k, v in sorted(p["tool_calls"].items()))
        tiers = "/".join(str(a["served_tiers"][t]) for t in ("1", "2", "3")) if a else "-"
        verdict = ("yes" if g["resolved"] else "no") + (" (edited tests)" if g["touched_tests"] else "")
        notes = (r.get("notes") or "").replace("|", "/")
        lines.append(
            f"| {r['task']} | {r['mode']} | {verdict} | {p['model_calls']} | {p['peak_context_tokens']} "
            f"| {p['total_prompt_tokens']} | {tools or '-'} | {tiers} | {a['escalations'] if a else '-'} "
            f"| {p['minutes']} | {notes} |"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def cmd_report(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    run_dir = RUNS_DIR / args.run_id
    results = [json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in sorted(run_dir.glob("*/*/result.json"))]
    if not results:
        print(f"[report] no collected results in {run_dir}")
        return 1
    text = render_report(results, args.run_id)
    RESULTS_FILE.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    print(f"[report] written to {RESULTS_FILE}")
    return 0


def cmd_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Show every task and whether each mode is prepared / collected in this run."""
    for task in load_tasks()["tasks"]:
        states = []
        for mode in MODES:
            d = run_dir_for(args.run_id, mode, task["id"])
            states.append(f"{mode}: {'collected' if (d / 'result.json').exists() else 'prepared' if d.exists() else '-'}")
        print(f"{task['id']:<24} {'   '.join(states)}")
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", default=DEFAULT_ENDPOINT, help="llama-server base URL")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("setup", help="clone pinned repos and create the test venv")
    sub.add_parser("validate", help="check each injected bug breaks its tests")
    sub.add_parser("doctor", help="check llama-server, Pi, and the ACC-MCP connection")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frozen setup (Phase 26): what a counted run was done with
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SETUP_FILE = "setup.json"
# Files whose uncommitted changes would make the recorded commit hash meaningless
FROZEN_PATHS = ("src", "eval/pi_bench.py", "eval/tasks.json", "eval/PROTOCOL.md", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock")


def _sha256(path: Path) -> str | None:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() if path.exists() else None


def model_quantization(name: str) -> str | None:
    """GGUF quantization from a model file or id, e.g. `Qwen3.5-4B-Q6_K.gguf` -> `Q6_K`."""
    m = re.search(r"(?i)(?<![A-Za-z0-9])(I?Q\d(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)*|BF16|F16|F32)(?![A-Za-z0-9])", name)
    return m.group(1).upper() if m else None


def collect_setup(endpoint: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything a counted run depends on: code version, model, server, agent, window, budget."""
    props = fetch_json(f"{endpoint}/props") or {}
    models = fetch_json(f"{endpoint}/v1/models") or {}
    model_id = ((models.get("data") or [{}])[0]).get("id", "")
    model_path = str(props.get("model_path") or "")
    try:
        window = int(props["default_generation_settings"]["n_ctx"])
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        window = None
    try:
        pi = subprocess.run(["pi", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        pi_version = pi.stdout.strip() or pi.stderr.strip() or None
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pi_version = None
    dirty = _git(PROJECT_ROOT, "status", "--porcelain", "--", *FROZEN_PATHS, check=False).stdout.strip()
    return {
        "frozen_at": datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "acc_mcp_commit": _git(PROJECT_ROOT, "rev-parse", "HEAD", check=False).stdout.strip() or None,
        "acc_mcp_dirty": bool(dirty),
        "model_id": model_id or None,
        "model_path": model_path or None,
        "quantization": model_quantization(model_path) or model_quantization(model_id),
        "llama_server_build": props.get("build_info"),
        "pi_version": pi_version,
        "context_window": window,
        "session_budget": session_budget_for(window) if window else None,
        "session_budget_share": SESSION_BUDGET_SHARE,
        "tasks_sha256": _sha256(TASKS_FILE),
        "protocol_sha256": _sha256(EVAL_DIR / "PROTOCOL.md"),
    }


def freeze_problems(setup: dict[str, Any], baselines: dict[str, dict[str, Any] | None]) -> list[str]:
    """Reasons the setup cannot be frozen for counted runs; empty when it can."""
    problems = []
    if setup["context_window"] is None:
        problems.append("llama-server /props is not reachable: start the model first")
    if not setup["acc_mcp_commit"]:
        problems.append("no git commit found for ACC-MCP")
    if setup["acc_mcp_dirty"]:
        problems.append(f"uncommitted changes in {', '.join(FROZEN_PATHS)}: commit them so the hash identifies the code")
    if not setup["pi_version"]:
        problems.append("`pi --version` failed: is Pi installed?")
    for repo, baseline in baselines.items():
        if baseline is None:
            problems.append(f"no baseline for {repo}: run `validate`")
        elif int(baseline.get("passed", 0)) == 0:
            problems.append(f"the clean {repo} suite passed 0 tests: run `setup` and `validate` again")
    return problems


def load_setup(run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    path = RUNS_DIR / run_id / SETUP_FILE
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if path.exists() else None


def cmd_freeze(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Record the setup of a run id once, before its first counted run."""
    path = RUNS_DIR / args.run_id / SETUP_FILE
    if path.exists() and not args.force:
        print(f"[freeze] {args.run_id} is already frozen ({path}); use a new --run-id, or --force to replace it")
        return 1
    setup = collect_setup(args.endpoint)
    baselines = {
        name: (json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if (p := BASELINE_DIR / f"{name}.json").exists() else None)
        for name in load_tasks()["repos"]
    }
    problems = freeze_problems(setup, baselines)
    if problems:
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"[freeze] NOT frozen: {problem}")
        return 1
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps({"run_id": args.run_id, **setup}, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(setup, indent=2))
    print(f"[freeze] {args.run_id} frozen in {path}")
    return 0


def check_frozen(run_id: str, context_window: int) -> str | None:
    """Why `prepare` must not continue under this run id (frozen setup changed), or None."""
    setup = load_setup(run_id)
    if setup is None:
        print(f"[prepare] warning: run {run_id!r} is not frozen; run `freeze --run-id {run_id}` before counted runs")
        return None
    if setup.get("context_window") != context_window:
        return f"context window is {context_window}, but {run_id} was frozen with {setup.get('context_window')}"
    if setup.get("tasks_sha256") != _sha256(TASKS_FILE):
        return f"eval/tasks.json changed since {run_id} was frozen"
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Report (Phase 26)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _median(values: list[float | None]) -> float | None:
    """Median of the measured values; None (shown as "–") when nothing was measured."""
    known = [v for v in values if v is not None]
    return round(statistics.median(known), 1) if known else None


def _fmt(value: Any) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return "–"
    return f"{value:g}" if isinstance(value, float) else str(value)


def _nav(result: dict[str, Any], key: str) -> Any:
    return (result.get("navigation") or {}).get(key)


def code_reading_tokens(result: dict[str, Any]) -> int | None:
    """Output tokens of the agent's own code reading plus ACC-MCP output (H1)."""
    classes = _nav(result, "tool_classes")
    return classes["code_read"]["tokens"] + classes["acc"]["tokens"] if classes else None


def summarize(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Counts and medians for one group of runs (one mode, or one mode and task kind)."""
    return {
        "runs": len(results),
        "resolved": sum(bool(r["grade"]["resolved"]) for r in results),
        "nav_before_edit": _median([_nav(r, "navigation_calls_before_target_edit") for r in results]),
        "target_edited": sum(bool(_nav(r, "target_edited")) for r in results),
        "code_reading_tokens": _median([code_reading_tokens(r) for r in results]),
        "wasted_reads": _median([_nav(r, "wasted_reads") for r in results]),
        "large_reads": sum(_nav(r, "large_reads") or 0 for r in results),
        "peak_context": _median([r["pi"]["peak_context_tokens"] for r in results]),
        "prompt_tokens": _median([r["pi"]["total_prompt_tokens"] for r in results]),
        "model_calls": _median([r["pi"]["model_calls"] for r in results]),
        "minutes": _median([r["pi"]["minutes"] for r in results]),
    }


def acc_summary(results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """ACC-MCP use and the decision model's online miss rate over all acc runs."""
    acc_runs = [r for r in results if r["mode"] == "acc"]
    ledgers = [r["acc"] for r in acc_runs if r.get("acc")]
    with_silent = [a for a in ledgers if a.get("silent_escalations") is not None]
    slices = sum(a["requests"] for a in with_silent)
    misses = sum(a["escalations"] + a["silent_escalations"] for a in with_silent)
    return {
        "runs": len(acc_runs),
        "used": sum(1 for a in ledgers if a["requests"]),
        "without_hint": sum(1 for r in acc_runs if r.get("hint") is False),
        "slices": sum(a["requests"] for a in ledgers),
        "served_tiers": {t: sum(a["served_tiers"][t] for a in ledgers) for t in ("1", "2", "3")},
        "model_tiers": {t: sum(a["model_tiers"][t] for a in ledgers) for t in ("1", "2", "3")},
        "explicit_escalations": sum(a["escalations"] for a in ledgers),
        "silent_escalations": sum(a["silent_escalations"] for a in with_silent) if with_silent else None,
        "online_miss_rate": round(misses / slices, 4) if slices else None,
    }


def _setup_lines(setup: dict[str, Any] | None) -> list[str]:
    if setup is None:
        return ["**Setup not frozen** (`freeze` was not run for this run id): these runs are not counted results.", ""]
    commit = (setup.get("acc_mcp_commit") or "?")[:12] + (" (with uncommitted changes)" if setup.get("acc_mcp_dirty") else "")
    budget = setup.get("session_budget")
    rows = [
        ("Frozen at", setup.get("frozen_at")),
        ("ACC-MCP commit", commit),
        ("Model", setup.get("model_id")),
        ("Model file", setup.get("model_path")),
        ("Quantization", setup.get("quantization")),
        ("llama-server build", setup.get("llama_server_build")),
        ("Pi", setup.get("pi_version")),
        ("Context window", setup.get("context_window")),
        ("Session budget", f"{budget} ({setup.get('session_budget_share', 0):.0%} of the window)" if budget else None),
        ("tasks.json / PROTOCOL.md sha256", f"{(setup.get('tasks_sha256') or '?')[:12]} / {(setup.get('protocol_sha256') or '?')[:12]}"),
    ]
    return ["| Item | Value |", "| :--- | :--- |", *(f"| {k} | {_fmt(v)} |" for k, v in rows), ""]


def _summary_table(groups: list[tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]], label: str) -> list[str]:
    lines = [
        f"| {label} | Runs | Resolved (H2) | Nav calls before target edit (H1) | Code-reading tokens (H1) "
        "| Wasted reads | Large reads (total) | Peak context (H3) | Prompt tokens | Model calls | Minutes |",
        "| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |",
    ]
    for name, rs in groups:
        if not rs:
            continue
        s = summarize(rs)
        lines.append(
            f"| {name} | {s['runs']} | {s['resolved']}/{s['runs']} | {_fmt(s['nav_before_edit'])} "
            f"| {_fmt(s['code_reading_tokens'])} | {_fmt(s['wasted_reads'])} | {s['large_reads']} "
            f"| {_fmt(s['peak_context'])} | {_fmt(s['prompt_tokens'])} | {_fmt(s['model_calls'])} | {_fmt(s['minutes'])} |"
        )
    return lines + [""]


def _pair(plain: Any, acc: Any) -> str:
    return f"{_fmt(plain)} / {_fmt(acc)}"


def render_run(results: list[dict[str, Any]], run_id: str, setup: dict[str, Any] | None,
               kinds: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
    """Markdown section for one run id: setup, summaries, ACC-MCP, paired and per-run tables."""
    for r in results:
        r.setdefault("kind", kinds.get(r["task"], "?"))
    by_mode = [(mode, [r for r in results if r["mode"] == mode]) for mode in MODES]
    lines = [f"## Run `{run_id}`", "", "### Setup", "", *_setup_lines(setup)]

    lines += ["### Summary per mode", "",
              "Medians over the runs of each mode, except Resolved and Large reads. – = not measured "
              "(for example, the target function was never edited).", "",
              *_summary_table(by_mode, "Mode")]
    by_kind = [(f"{kind} / {mode}", [r for r in rs if r["kind"] == kind])
               for kind in ("direct", "call_graph") for mode, rs in by_mode]
    lines += ["### Summary per task kind", "",
              "`call_graph` tasks name an entry function whose helper has the bug (`eval/PROTOCOL.md` 4.1).", "",
              *_summary_table(by_kind, "Kind / mode")]

    a = acc_summary(results)
    if a["runs"]:
        tiers = "/".join(str(a["served_tiers"][t]) for t in ("1", "2", "3"))
        picked = "/".join(str(a["model_tiers"][t]) for t in ("1", "2", "3"))
        lines += [
            "### ACC-MCP", "",
            f"- Called in **{a['used']} of {a['runs']}** acc runs ({a['without_hint']} without the hint sentence).",
            f"- Slices served: {a['slices']}; tiers 1/2/3 served = {tiers}, picked by the decision model = {picked}.",
            f"- Escalations: {a['explicit_escalations']} explicit (`min_tier`), {_fmt(a['silent_escalations'])} silent; "
            f"online miss rate **{_fmt(a['online_miss_rate'])}** (explicit + silent / slices, runs with line ranges only).",
            "",
        ]

    lines += ["### Paired per task (plain / acc)", "",
              "| Task | Kind | Resolved | Nav calls before target edit | Code-reading tokens | Wasted reads "
              "| Peak context | ACC tiers 1/2/3 | Escalations explicit / silent |",
              "| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |"]
    for task in sorted({r["task"] for r in results}):
        plain = next((r for r in results if r["task"] == task and r["mode"] == "plain"), None)
        acc = next((r for r in results if r["task"] == task and r["mode"] == "acc"), None)

        def get(r: dict[str, Any] | None, fn: Any) -> Any:
            return fn(r) if r else None

        ledger = acc.get("acc") if acc else None
        lines.append(
            f"| {task} | {(plain or acc)['kind']} "
            f"| {_pair(get(plain, lambda r: 'yes' if r['grade']['resolved'] else 'no'), get(acc, lambda r: 'yes' if r['grade']['resolved'] else 'no'))} "
            f"| {_pair(get(plain, lambda r: _nav(r, 'navigation_calls_before_target_edit')), get(acc, lambda r: _nav(r, 'navigation_calls_before_target_edit')))} "
            f"| {_pair(get(plain, code_reading_tokens), get(acc, code_reading_tokens))} "
            f"| {_pair(get(plain, lambda r: _nav(r, 'wasted_reads')), get(acc, lambda r: _nav(r, 'wasted_reads')))} "
            f"| {_pair(get(plain, lambda r: r['pi']['peak_context_tokens']), get(acc, lambda r: r['pi']['peak_context_tokens']))} "
            f"| {'/'.join(str(ledger['served_tiers'][t]) for t in ('1', '2', '3')) if ledger else '–'} "
            f"| {_pair(ledger['escalations'], ledger.get('silent_escalations')) if ledger else '–'} |"
        )

    lines += ["", "### Every run", "",
              "| Task | Mode | Hint | Resolved | Calls | Peak ctx | Prompt tokens | Tools used | Min | Notes |",
              "| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | :---: | :--- |"]
    for r in sorted(results, key=lambda r: (r["task"], r["mode"])):
        p, g = r["pi"], r["grade"]
        tools = ", ".join(f"{k.replace(ACC_PREFIX, 'acc:')}×{v}" for k, v in sorted(p["tool_calls"].items()))
        verdict = ("yes" if g["resolved"] else "no") + (" (edited tests)" if g.get("touched_tests") else "")
        hint = "–" if r["mode"] == "plain" else ("yes" if r.get("hint") else "no")
        notes = (r.get("notes") or "").replace("|", "/").replace("\n", " ")
        lines.append(
            f"| {r['task']} | {r['mode']} | {hint} | {verdict} | {p['model_calls']} | {p['peak_context_tokens']} "
            f"| {p['total_prompt_tokens']} | {tools or '–'} | {p['minutes']} | {notes} |"
        )
    return lines + [""]


def render_report(runs: list[tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any] | None]], kinds: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """eval/results.md: one section per run id, every run reported (PROTOCOL.md section 9)."""
    lines = [
        "# Pi Benchmark Results", "",
        "Plain Pi vs Pi + ACC-MCP, operated by hand in interactive Pi (method and hypotheses H1-H3: "
        "`eval/PROTOCOL.md`). The pilot session (`run1`) is not part of the results.", "",
        "- **H1 (navigation cost):** navigation calls before the first edit of the target function, and "
        "code-reading tokens (the agent's own `read`/`grep`/`sed`/... output plus ACC-MCP slices; characters / 3.8 "
        "for both modes).",
        "- **H2 (success):** resolved tasks.",
        "- **H3 (peak context):** largest prompt of one model call, as llama-server reported it to Pi.", "",
    ]
    for run_id, results, setup in runs:
        lines += render_run(results, run_id, setup, kinds)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def cmd_report(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    kinds = {t["id"]: t.get("kind", "?") for t in load_tasks()["tasks"]}
    runs = []
    for run_id in args.run_id or [DEFAULT_RUN_ID]:
        run_dir = RUNS_DIR / run_id
        results = [json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for p in sorted(run_dir.glob("*/*/result.json"))]
        if not results:
            print(f"[report] no collected results in {run_dir}")
            return 1
        runs.append((run_id, results, load_setup(run_id)))
    text = render_report(runs, kinds)
    RESULTS_FILE.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(text)
    print(f"[report] written to {RESULTS_FILE}")
    return 0
